narr: Eastern Pacific Hurricane Hilary made landfall on the Baja Peninsula early on the morning of the 20th and reached Southern California as a tropical storm that afternoon. The cyclone brought widespread flash flooding to southeast California, along with isolated high winds.
ev: Water and debris flooded Highway 190 between mile markers 45 and 46.
The intersection of Highways 190 and 136 was washed out. The road remained closed and intermittently flooded for over a day.
Highway 395 flooded both in Lone Pine and at Boulder Creek 4 miles SSE of Lone Pine.
Rocks and debris blocked Highway 190 at Towne Pass.

Major flash flooding occurred throughout Death Valley National Park. Four hundred miles of NPS roads were damaged or destroyed, in addition to other roads maintained by the county and state. About 1000 feet of fresh water lines were destroyed at Furnace Creek. Damage to most structures was minimized or prevented by berms and other protections. The exact start and end times are unknown.
Flash flooding occurred throughout the Mojave National Preserve. All roads, facilities, trails, etc in the preserve were closed. Exact start and end times unknown.
Heavy flooding pushed debris across Highway 62 between Cactus Jack and Godwin.
Mud and debris washed onto Highway 62 just east of Olympic Rd.
Several roads in Twentynine Palms were closed due to flooding.
A boulder washed onto Highway 62 at Hess Rd.
Flash flooding in Baker was up to vehicle hoods.
Highway 95 was flooded near mile marker 17.
The intersection of Highway 178 and Trona Rd was flooded with multiple vehicles stuck, and 178 was also possibly washed out at Pinnacle Rd.
Water and mud covered La Contenta and Alta Loma Rds.
Four feet of rushing water trapped people in their cars on Highway 127. The road was severely damaged.
Mud and debris covered the intersection of Amboy Rd and Cactus Jack.
The intersection of Highway 395 and Randsburg Cutoff Rd was flooded.
Fast-moving water covered the intersection of I-15 and Fort Irwin Rd.
Highway 247 was flooded and closed at Pipes Canyon Rd.
A vehicle was covered in mud and sinking at the intersection of Covington Dr and East Dr.
Two feet of rock and debris covered Highway 62 near Valley View Rd, and small boulders were on the highway from Senilis Ave to east of Valley View Rd.

Fast flowing water, rock, and debris covered Whitney Portal Rd, the Whitney Portal parking lots, and the road to Lone Pine Campground. Whitney Portal Rd was destroyed by high flows in Lone Pine Creek.

A slide of mud and gravel covered Highway 395 at Ash Creek Rd. Mud flowed heavily along the side of the highway and into part of the southbound lanes. Due to ongoing flooding in multiple places, Highway 395 was eventually closed all the way from Bishop to Pearsonville overnight.
